simple.meaning: שֶׁסַע (sheçaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a fissure.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Leviticus, Deuteronomy, beginning at Leviticus 11:3. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֶׁסַע (H8157) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שֶׁסַע (sheçaʻ) / H8157 is traced through Leviticus 11:3, Leviticus 11:7, Leviticus 11:26, Deuteronomy 14:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat.

timeline.evidenceText: Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat.
The pig, because it has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, is unclean to you.
“ ‘Every animal which has a split hoof that isn’t completely divided, or doesn’t chew the cud, is unclean to you. Everyone who touches them shall be unclean.
Every animal that parts the hoof, and has the hoof split in two and chews the cud, among the animals, you may eat.
